48.watch: Remember that this rule is only about proving the notice was sent, not about whether the recipient actually read it.

49.summary: This rule explains how the expenses for holding meetings of creditors or contributories are paid. These costs are paid directly using the money or property belonging to the company. The text is short and simple, meaning no extra details are provided.
points: Meetings of creditors or contributories must be convened and conducted.
The expenses for these meetings are paid using the company's assets.
49.example: Meera Textiles Private Limited is going through a winding up process. The company needs to hold a meeting with its creditors to discuss financial matters. To pay for the venue, notices, and other arrangements of this meeting, the organizers use the existing assets and funds belonging to Meera Textiles Private Limited, strictly following the rule.

terms.meaning: People or businesses that the company owes money to.
People who are liable to contribute to the assets of the company in the event of its winding up.
The property, money, and valuable items owned by the company.

49.watch: People often assume that the person calling the meeting must pay out of pocket, but the rule states the costs come from the company's assets.

50.summary: The text explains who leads the meeting when a company is winding up. Either the Company Liquidator or someone chosen by them will run the meeting. This choice must be made using a specific official form.
points: The Company Liquidator can act as the Chairman of the meeting.
The Company Liquidator can also nominate another person to be the Chairman.
Any nomination for the Chairman must be made in Form WIN 32.
50.example: At ABC Logistics Private Limited, the winding up process has begun. The Company Liquidator cannot attend the upcoming creditor meeting personally. To ensure the meeting runs smoothly, the Liquidator decides to nominate an assistant named Rahul to lead it. The Liquidator fills out Form WIN 32 to make this official. Rahul then acts as the Chairman of the meeting, following the exact rules set for the company's closure.

terms.meaning: An official person appointed to wind up or close down a company's business.
A specific official document or paper used for this legal process.

50.watch: Do not confuse the person chosen as Chairman with the Company Liquidator, as the Liquidator can delegate this role to someone else.

52.summary: This rule explains how a decision is passed during a meeting of contributories. A decision is considered passed if it gets support from a majority of the value of members who are present and voting. The voting value is decided by the number of votes each member is allowed to have under the law or the company rules.
points: A resolution passes when a majority in value of the members voting are in favour.
Members can be present personally or by proxy.
The voting value is based on the votes each member is entitled to under the Act or articles.
52.example: At a meeting of Green Agro Private Limited, a vote was held on a resolution. Two contributories attended. Contributory A had a voting value of one hundred votes, and Contributory B had a voting value of fifty votes. Contributory A voted in favour, while Contributory B voted against. Because Contributory A held the majority in value of the votes cast, the resolution was successfully passed.

terms.meaning: Persons liable to contribute to the assets of a company in the event of its winding up.
A person authorized to vote on behalf of another member at a meeting.
The rulebook of a company that governs its internal management.

52.watch: Remember that the majority is based on the financial value of votes, not just a simple count of people.

53.summary: This rule requires the person winding up a company to file certified copies of certain resolutions in the Tribunal. The court registry must then keep these resolutions in a specific file for that case. It helps maintain a proper official record of decisions made during the winding up process.
points: The Company Liquidator must file a certified copy of every resolution.
The resolution must be from a meeting of the creditors or contributories.
The filing must be done in the Tribunal.
The Registry keeps a file of these resolutions for each case.
53.example: Meera Textiles Private Limited is going through a winding up process. During a meeting, the creditors pass a formal decision regarding the company's debts. The Company Liquidator, Mr. Sharma, creates a copy of this decision and certifies it with his signature. He then submits this certified copy to the Tribunal. Finally, the Tribunal's Registry places this document into the official case file for Meera Textiles Private Limited to keep a proper record.

terms.meaning: The person appointed to handle the winding up and closing of a company.
People or businesses to whom the company owes money.
People who are required to contribute to the assets of a company during its winding up.

53.watch: Do not confuse the Company Liquidator with the company's regular managers, as this rule applies specifically to the person handling the winding up.

54.summary: This rule says that a meeting of creditors or contributories remains valid even if some people did not receive their notice. However, the Tribunal can order differently if it chooses. This ensures that a meeting can still go ahead successfully despite minor delivery issues.
points: A meeting of creditors or contributories is summoned by notice.
Proceedings and resolutions at the meeting are valid even if some did not receive the notice.
The Tribunal has the power to order otherwise.
54.example: Meera Textiles Private Limited held a meeting of its creditors to discuss winding up matters. Notices were sent out to everyone as required. Due to a postal delay, two creditors did not get their notices on time and missed the meeting. The other creditors attended and passed a resolution. Because of this rule, the meeting and its resolution remain legally valid, unless the Tribunal decides to give a different order.

terms.meaning: People who are liable to contribute to the assets of a company in the event of its being wound up.
The judicial body or authority that handles company law matters, such as the National Company Law Tribunal.

54.watch: Do not assume that missing notices always cancel the meeting, because the rule keeps the proceedings valid unless the Tribunal orders otherwise.

55.summary: This rule explains how a meeting can be delayed or postponed. The person leading the meeting, called the chairman, can delay it if the people attending agree. The next meeting must happen in the same place unless a new location is chosen or the court gives different instructions.
points: The chairman can adjourn the meeting with the agreement of the creditors or contributories present.
The adjourned meeting must take place at the same location as the original meeting.
A different location can be used if the adjournment resolution names one, or if the Tribunal orders it.
55.example: At a meeting for Meera Textiles Private Limited, the members could not finish all their discussions. Mr. Sharma, the chairman, asked the creditors present if they agreed to postpone the meeting to a later date. Everyone consented. Since the resolution did not name a new venue and the Tribunal gave no other orders, Mr. Sharma announced that the adjourned meeting would be held at the exact same conference hall as the original meeting.

terms.meaning: To pause or postpone a meeting to a later time.
A specialized legal authority or court that handles specific types of cases.

55.watch: Do not assume you can change the meeting location without a specific resolution or Tribunal order.

56.summary: This rule explains the minimum number of people needed for a company winding up meeting to start and make decisions. If enough people do not show up, the meeting must be moved to another day. If the new meeting still lacks enough people, special steps are taken.
points: A creditors meeting needs at least three voting creditors, or all of them if there are three or fewer.
A contributories meeting needs at least three contributories, or all of them if there are three or fewer.
If no proper group is present within half an hour, the meeting moves to the same day and time next week.
At the moved meeting, at least two people present in person can run the meeting.
If even two people are not at the moved meeting, the chairman must report to the Tribunal.
56.example: At Star Electronics Private Limited, a meeting for contributories is scheduled. Only two contributories arrive within the first thirty minutes. Because this is fewer than the required three, the chairman delays the meeting to the same time next week. When next week arrives, only one contributory shows up. Since this is still below the minimum of two for an adjourned meeting, the chairman prepares a report and submits it to the Tribunal to ask for further directions.

terms.meaning: Persons liable to contribute to the assets of a company in the event of its being wound up.
The minimum number of members needed to be present to legally conduct a meeting.
The authority dealing with company law matters and disputes.

56.watch: Remember that the rules for attendance change if the meeting is delayed to the following week.

59.summary: This rule tells us when a creditor is not allowed to vote on a company's debt matters. Creditors cannot vote if their debt amount is uncertain, not yet finalized, or depends on a future event. There is also a special condition for creditors holding certain notes or bills.
points: A creditor cannot vote if the debt is unliquidated, contingent, or its value is not ascertained.
A creditor holding a current bill of exchange or promissory note cannot vote unless they follow a specific rule.
They must treat certain prior liable persons' liability as a security and estimate its value.
They must deduct that estimated value from their proof of debt only for voting purposes, not for dividends.
59.example: Aarav owed money to Riya Enterprises Private Limited and held a promissory note. When the company faced winding up, Riya wanted to vote on the debt. However, the exact value of the debt was not yet ascertained, and Riya held a bill of exchange. According to the rules, Riya could not vote on this uncalculated debt unless she estimated the value of prior liabilities, treated them as security, and deducted that amount specifically for voting purposes.

terms.meaning: A debt whose exact amount is not yet decided or depends on a future uncertain event happening.

terms.term: bill of exchange or promissory note
terms.meaning: A written signed promise or order to pay a certain sum of money to a specific person.
A share of the company's money given to creditors or shareholders.

59.watch: Do not confuse voting rules with dividend calculations, as deductions made for voting do not apply to dividends.

60.summary: This rule explains how a secured creditor can vote during the winding up of a company by the Tribunal. Unless the creditor gives up their security, they must provide specific details and the value of their security assessed by a registered valuer. They are allowed to vote only for the remaining amount owed to them after subtracting that value.
points: A secured creditor must state the particulars and date of their security in their proof.
The security must be valued by a registered valuer.
The creditor can vote only for the balance amount left after deducting the value of the security.
These steps apply unless the creditor chooses to surrender their security.
60.example: Alpha Textiles Private Limited is undergoing winding up by the Tribunal. Beta Finance is a secured creditor holding a mortgage. Instead of surrendering the mortgage, Beta Finance submits its proof of debt, including the security details and a valuation report from a registered valuer. The total debt is one lakh rupees, and the security is valued at forty thousand rupees. Beta Finance is entitled to vote only in respect of the balance due, which is sixty thousand rupees.

terms.meaning: A lender who holds a security, such as a mortgage or charge, over the company's property or assets.
The legal process of closing down a company and settling its affairs.
A professional officially registered to determine the value of assets.

60.watch: A secured creditor cannot vote on the full amount of their debt unless they completely surrender their security first.

61.summary: Under this rule, if a secured creditor votes on their entire debt, they are generally treated as giving up their security. However, the Tribunal can save them from this if the creditor applies and proves they forgot to value the security by mistake. This protects creditors who made an honest error.
points: Voting on the whole debt means surrendering the security.
The Tribunal can make an exception upon an application.
The exception applies only if missing the value was due to inadvertence.
61.example: Meera Textiles Private Limited faced winding up. A secured creditor, ABC Bank, voted on its whole debt without mentioning its security. Realizing the mistake, ABC Bank quickly filed an application with the Tribunal. The Tribunal found that the omission was a pure accident caused by inadvertence, so the bank was not deemed to have surrendered its security.

terms.meaning: a lender who holds a claim backed by company assets or property
given up or let go of rights
an honest mistake or oversight

61.watch: A common confusion is thinking the security is lost forever without realizing the Tribunal can fix honest mistakes.

62.summary: When a secured creditor votes in a meeting using their estimated value of a security, the liquidator can ask them to hand over that security for all creditors. The liquidator must pay the estimated value to take the security, and can ask the Tribunal for an order if needed. The Tribunal may sometimes allow the creditor to fix their valuation before handing it over.
points: The liquidator has fifteen days from the meeting to ask the creditor to give up the security.
The liquidator must pay the estimated value of the security for the general benefit of creditors.
The liquidator can apply to the Tribunal to force the creditor to give up the security if necessary.
The Tribunal may allow the creditor to correct their valuation for a good reason upon terms as to costs.
62.example: Meera Textiles Private Limited went into liquidation. Creditor Rohan held a machine as security and voted in a meeting after valuing it. Within fifteen days, the liquidator asked Rohan to hand over the machine for all creditors by paying that estimated value. Rohan refused, so the liquidator applied to the Tribunal for an order. Rohan showed a good cause to the Tribunal, which permitted him to correct his valuation before giving up the security upon just terms for costs.

terms.meaning: a person appointed to wind up the affairs of a company
a lender who holds a security or charge over the company's property
the judicial body that handles company law cases in India

62.watch: Note that the fifteen-day limit starts from the date of the meeting where the creditor voted, not from any other date.

63.summary: The person leading a meeting has the power to accept or reject a proof for voting purposes. Their decision can be challenged through an appeal to the Tribunal. If the leader is unsure, they must mark the proof as objected to and let the creditor vote, subject to later invalidation if the objection is sustained.
points: The chairman decides whether to accept or reject a proof for voting.
A decision by the chairman can be appealed to the Tribunal.
If in doubt, the chairman marks the proof as objected to and allows the creditor to vote.
The vote becomes invalid if the objection is sustained later.
63.example: At a meeting for Alpha Solutions Private Limited, the chairman faced a tricky proof submitted by creditor Rohan. Unsure if it was valid, the chairman marked the proof as objected to and allowed Rohan to cast his vote. Later, if the Tribunal or proper authority sustains the objection, Rohan's vote will be declared invalid.

terms.meaning: The person in charge of running the meeting.
A legal body or authority that handles disputes and appeals.

63.watch: Do not assume the vote is final if marked as objected to, as it can be declared invalid later.

64.summary: This rule explains how records must be kept after a company meeting. The chairman must write down what happened in the meeting and put it in a special book within thirty days. A list of everyone who attended must also be made and kept safely.
points: The chairman must write the minutes of the meeting.
Minutes must be entered in the Minute Book within 30 days.
The minutes must be signed by the chairman of that meeting or the next meeting.
A list of creditors and contributories present must be kept in Form WIN 33.
64.example: Mr. Sharma acted as the chairman for a meeting held for Apex Solutions Private Limited. Within thirty days, he made sure the minutes of the proceedings were drawn up and fairly entered in the Minute Book. He then signed the minutes. Along with this, a separate list of all the creditors and contributories who attended the meeting was carefully made and kept in Form WIN 33, exactly as required by the rule.

terms.meaning: The official written record of what was said and decided at a meeting.
People or companies that are owed money by the company.
People who are liable to contribute to the assets of the company if it is wound up.

64.watch: People often confuse who can sign the minutes, but the rule allows either the current chairman or the chairman of the next meeting to sign them.

65.summary: This rule tells the Company Liquidator to inform the Tribunal about the outcome of a meeting. The report must be sent within seven days of the meeting ending. It uses a specific official form called Form No. WIN 34.
points: The Company Liquidator must report the meeting result to the Tribunal.
The report must be submitted in Form No. WIN 34.
The deadline is within seven days after the meeting finishes.
65.example: Meera Textiles Private Limited is undergoing winding up. The Company Liquidator holds a meeting with the creditors and contributories to discuss important matters. Once the meeting concludes successfully, the Liquidator prepares the final result of the meeting in Form No. WIN 34. To follow the rule strictly, the Liquidator submits this official report to the Tribunal within seven days from the day the meeting ended.

terms.meaning: The person appointed to manage the winding up and closing down of a company.
The legal authority or court handling company law matters in India.
People who are liable to contribute to the assets of the company in the event of its winding up.

65.watch: Remember that the seven-day countdown starts right after the meeting finishes, not when the notice is sent.

67.summary: This rule explains how a creditor or contributory can give a proxy to someone else. They can give either a general proxy using Form WIN 35 or a special proxy using Form WIN 36. Anyone can be chosen to act as this proxy.
points: A creditor or contributory may appoint any person to be their proxy.
Proxies can be either general or special.
A general proxy must use Form WIN 35.
A special proxy must use Form WIN 36.
67.example: Meera Textiles Private Limited is going through a winding up process. Rohit, a creditor of the company, cannot attend a meeting in person. To ensure his interests are represented, Rohit decides to give a proxy to his friend Aman. Since Rohit wants Aman to handle a specific matter, he fills out Form WIN 36 to make Aman his special proxy.

terms.meaning: A person or company to whom money is owed.
A person liable to contribute to the assets of a company in the event of its being wound up.
A person authorized to act on behalf of someone else.

67.watch: Do not confuse a general proxy with a special proxy, as each requires a different specific form.

68.summary: This rule allows a creditor or contributory in a company winding up to appoint certain officials as their proxy. You can choose either the Company Liquidator or the chairman of the meeting to act for you. This proxy can be general or special.
points: Applies to a creditor or a contributory.
Applies when a company is being wound up by the Tribunal.
You can appoint the Company Liquidator as your proxy.
If there is no Company Liquidator, you can appoint the chairman of the meeting as your proxy.
68.example: Meera Textiles Private Limited is going through a winding up process ordered by the Tribunal. Rahul is a creditor of this company who cannot attend the upcoming meeting in person. Since there is no Company Liquidator appointed yet, Rahul decides to appoint the chairman of the meeting to act as his special proxy to represent his interests and vote on his behalf during the proceedings.

terms.meaning: a person or business to whom the company owes money
a person liable to contribute to the assets of the company in the event of its being wound up
a person authorized to act on behalf of another person, especially in voting

68.watch: Do not assume you can appoint just anyone as a proxy under this specific rule, as it is limited to the Company Liquidator or the chairman.

69.summary: This rule explains what happens when a Company Liquidator cannot attend a meeting where they hold proxies. The liquidator can give written permission to someone under their official control to use those proxies instead. That person must use the proxies exactly as the liquidator directs.
points: A Company Liquidator may hold proxies for a meeting.
If the liquidator cannot attend the meeting, they can choose someone else to go.
The replacement must be someone under the liquidator's official control.
The liquidator must give this permission in writing and direct how the proxies are used.
69.example: Meera Textiles Private Limited is undergoing winding up. Mr. Roy, the Company Liquidator, holds several proxies for an upcoming meeting but falls ill and cannot attend. Following the rules, Mr. Roy writes a formal note deputing his assistant, Ms. Sen, who works under his official control. He gives her clear written directions on how to vote using the proxies on his behalf at the meeting.

terms.meaning: A person authorized to act for another, or the written document granting that authority.
The person appointed to handle the winding up and closing of a company.
To appoint someone to act on one's behalf.

69.watch: Make sure to note that the helper must be under the liquidator's official control and receive written instructions.

70.summary: When sending a notice to call a meeting of creditors and contributories under the Companies (Winding Up) Rules, 2020, the company must also send forms of proxies along with it. No specific name can be pre-printed or inserted into these proxy forms before they are sent out. This ensures that the people voting have complete freedom to choose who represents them.
points: Send proxy forms along with the meeting notice to creditors and contributories.
Do not insert or print any name in the proxy form before sending it.
70.example: Meera Textiles Private Limited is preparing a meeting for its creditors and contributories. The company manager sends out the notices for the meeting. Along with each notice, the manager includes a blank form of proxy. To be fair, the manager makes sure that no pre-filled names of any representatives are printed on these forms, allowing the creditors and contributories to freely fill in whoever they wish.

terms.meaning: A person authorized to represent someone else, or the form used to appoint that person.
Persons liable to contribute to the assets of a company in the event of its being wound up.

70.watch: Do not pre-fill any names on the proxy forms before sending them to the participants.

71.summary: This rule explains when and where a proxy must be submitted in a company winding up process. A proxy is a document that lets someone else vote or act on your behalf. You must give this document to the Company Liquidator at least 48 hours before the meeting starts.
points: A proxy must be lodged before the meeting.
The deadline is not later than 48 hours before the meeting.
It must be given to the Company Liquidator.
This rule applies to a winding up ordered by the Tribunal.
71.example: Meera Textiles Private Limited is going through a winding up process ordered by the Tribunal. Rahul is a creditor who cannot attend the upcoming meeting in person. He decides to appoint his friend Amit to attend and vote for him. To do this legally, Rahul fills out a proxy form. He makes sure to lodge this proxy form with the Company Liquidator exactly 55 hours before the meeting begins, which meets the requirement of doing it not later than 48 hours before the meeting.

terms.meaning: A person authorized to act for another, or the written document granting that authority.
The official person appointed to manage the winding up of a company.
A specialized legal body that handles company disputes and winding up cases.

71.watch: Make sure to submit the proxy to the Company Liquidator, not to any other company officer.

72.summary: This rule stops anyone holding a voting proxy from voting for a resolution that gives them, their partner, or their boss extra money from the company's assets. They can only receive money if they are a creditor sharing equally with all other creditors. This keeps voting fair and prevents people from using proxies for personal financial gain.
points: Applies to anyone acting under a general or special proxy.
Bans voting in favour of resolutions that give direct or indirect financial benefits.
Prohibits remuneration from company assets to the proxy holder, partner, or employer.
Allows payment only if they are a regular creditor getting paid ratably with others.
72.example: At ABC Limited, Rajesh is holding a proxy to vote on behalf of a major investor during the winding up process. A resolution is proposed to grant special consulting fees directly to Rajesh's business partner using the company's remaining assets. Because this rule strictly forbids proxy holders from voting for resolutions that financially benefit their partners, Rajesh cannot vote in favour of this resolution. He may only receive money if he or his partner acts as a standard creditor sharing equally alongside all other creditors.

terms.meaning: A person authorized to vote on behalf of someone else.
Money paid for work or a service.
Distributed proportionally or in equal portions among people.

72.watch: People often confuse being a regular creditor with getting special payments outside the standard sharing process.

73.summary: This rule simply says that a minor cannot be chosen to act as a proxy. A proxy is someone who represents another person. This applies to both general and special types of proxies.
points: Minors are not allowed to be general proxies.
Minors are not allowed to be special proxies.
73.example: Aarav wanted to appoint someone to represent him at a company meeting using a proxy form. He asked his 16-year-old nephew, Rohan, to be his special proxy. Because Rohan is a minor, this appointment is not allowed under the rule.

terms.meaning: A person who has not reached the age of majority.
A person authorized to act on behalf of another person.

73.watch: People often get confused about whether special proxies have different age rules, but this rule applies to both general and special proxies.

74.summary: This rule explains how a proxy can be accepted when the person giving it is blind or cannot write. A witness must be present to write the details and sign the document. The blind or incapable person can then add their signature or mark.
points: Applies to a creditor or contributory who is blind or cannot write.
A witness must write all the insertions in the proxy.
The witness must write their description and address.
The witness must add a certificate at the bottom stating they wrote it at the person's request and in their presence.
74.example: Mr. Sharma, a creditor of Meera Textiles Private Limited, is completely blind and cannot write. He wants to appoint a proxy for a meeting. His neighbor, Mr. Verma, acts as the witness. Mr. Verma writes all the required details into the proxy form at Mr. Sharma's request and in his presence. Mr. Verma then adds his own name, description, and address, along with a certificate at the bottom of the proxy. Finally, Mr. Sharma places his thumb mark on the document, and the proxy is successfully accepted.

terms.meaning: A person or company to whom money is owed.
A person liable to contribute to the assets of a company in the event of its winding up.
A person authorized to vote on behalf of another person, or the written document used for this purpose.

74.watch: Make sure the witness writes all insertions and adds their certificate before the creditor or contributory signs or makes their mark.

75.summary: This rule explains how a proxy can sign for a creditor or contributory who does not know English. The proxy form must follow the standard process, and a witness must certify that it was explained in a language the person understands. Additionally, the witness must write the person's name in English below their signature.
points: Applies to creditors or contributories who do not know English.
The proxy must be executed according to rule 74.
A witness must certify that the proxy was explained in a known language.
The witness must write the person's name in English under the signature.
75.example: Aarav owns shares in Aarav Textiles Private Limited and is considered a contributory, but he only speaks Hindi and does not know English. When he wants to appoint a proxy for a meeting, he cannot just sign a standard English form. Instead, the proxy is filled out and executed under rule 74. A witness fluent in Hindi explains the document to Aarav, signs a certificate stating it was explained in his language, and clearly writes Aarav's name in English beneath Aarav's signature.

terms.meaning: A person or company to whom money is owed.
A person liable to contribute to the assets of a company in the event of its winding up.
A person authorized to act on behalf of another, or the written document appointing that person.

75.watch: Do not forget that the witness must write the person's name in English below the signature.

77.summary: Sometimes a person winding up a company needs extra help to do the job. The Official Liquidator must ask the Tribunal for permission to hire this special or additional staff. The Tribunal can then approve the staff and decide their pay and allowances.
points: The Official Liquidator decides if extra staff is needed for a liquidation.
The Official Liquidator must apply to the Tribunal to get permission for hiring.
The Tribunal has the power to sanction the staff.
The Tribunal decides the salaries and allowances for the approved staff.
77.example: Meera Textiles Private Limited is going through a winding up process. The Official Liquidator finds that the company's financial records are too complex and realizes that extra accountants are needed to handle the work. Since the Official Liquidator cannot hire them directly, an application is submitted to the Tribunal for permission. The Tribunal reviews the request and grants sanction for the special staff, while also setting their salaries and allowances.

terms.meaning: An officer appointed to manage the winding up and closing of a company.
A specialized legal body or court that handles company law cases.
Official approval or permission.

77.watch: Do not assume the Official Liquidator can set staff salaries; only the Tribunal decides the pay and allowances.

79.summary: This rule requires the person winding up a company to keep a special record book for that specific business. Inside this book, they must write down details of all meetings, court orders, and important administrative actions. This helps provide a clear and accurate picture of how the company's affairs are being managed.
points: A separate record book must be maintained for each company.
Minutes of all meetings involving creditors, contributories, or the advisory committee must be entered.
The substance of all orders passed by the Tribunal during liquidation must be included.
All non-account matters necessary to show a correct view of the administration must be recorded.
79.example: Aarav is appointed as the Company Liquidator for Apex Technologies Private Limited. To follow the rules, Aarav starts a brand new physical record book dedicated only to this company. During their first meeting with the creditors, Aarav carefully writes down the minutes and the resolutions passed. Later, when the Tribunal passes an order regarding the company, Aarav enters the substance of that order into the same book to ensure everything is properly documented.

terms.meaning: The person responsible for winding up or closing down a company.
Persons liable to contribute to the assets of a company in the event of its being wound up.
The judicial authority handling company law matters in India.

79.watch: Do not confuse matters of account with the administrative and meeting records that must go into this specific book.

80.summary: This rule requires the person winding up a company to maintain specific financial books, cash books, and registers as applicable. They must also keep any other necessary office books and update incomplete accounts quickly. If the business continues to run, separate books must be kept and checked regularly.
points: The Company Liquidator must maintain specific registers and books like cash books, ledgers, and asset registers.
The liquidator must also keep extra office books like a petty cash register and correspondence register for efficient work.
If company accounts are incomplete when the winding up order is made, the liquidator must complete them quickly.
If authorized to run the business, the liquidator must keep separate trading books and verify them at least once a month.
Proper vouchers with serial numbers must be kept for all payments and expenses.
80.example: Aarav is appointed as the Company Liquidator for Apex Technologies Private Limited. Following the rules, Aarav starts maintaining the Central Cash Book and Register of Assets. Since Apex Technologies had incomplete financial records, Aarav works to bring them up to date. Aarav also collects all payment receipts and numbers them serially to ensure every expense is properly recorded during the winding up process.

terms.meaning: The person appointed to wind up the affairs of a company.
A book keeping financial accounts.
A receipt or document showing proof of payment or expense.

80.watch: Do not assume specific penalties or strict deadlines beyond what the text states.

81.summary: The Company Liquidator must deposit all money and cheques received for the company into a special bank account by the next working day. A small amount of petty cash can be kept for daily expenses, and larger payments must be made by cheque. Additionally, the liquidator has to submit quarterly reports and bank statements to the Tribunal.
points: Deposit all money, cheques, and drafts into a special bank account by the next working day.
Do not make deductions from the daily realisations before depositing them.
Keep a petty cash fund for daily expenses and pay amounts above two thousand rupees by cheque.
Send quarterly reports and bank statements of the special account to the Tribunal.
81.example: Aarav is the Company Liquidator for Apex Engineering Private Limited. On Monday, he receives a cheque for the company. By Tuesday, which is the next working day, he deposits the full amount into the special bank account without making any deductions. To pay for small office supplies, he uses his permitted petty cash. For a larger bill of three thousand rupees, he writes a cheque drawn against the special bank account. Every quarter, Aarav submits his bank statements and a report to the Tribunal.

terms.meaning: The person appointed to wind up a company and handle its money and assets.
A bank listed under the second schedule of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934.
The judicial authority that oversees company law matters, such as the National Company Law Tribunal.

81.watch: A common confusion is whether the liquidator can keep some cash from daily collections before depositing, but the rule states that all realisations must be deposited without deduction.

82.summary: This rule explains what the Company Liquidator must do with financial papers like bills and cheques that belong to the company under winding up. As soon as the Liquidator receives them, they must be deposited in the bank to collect the money. Once the money is collected, the bank puts it into a special bank account.
points: All bills, cheques, hundies, notes, and other securities payable to the company or its Liquidator must be handled promptly.
The Company Liquidator must deposit these items into the bank as soon as they receive them.
The bank presents them for acceptance and payment, or just payment.
Once the money is collected, the bank credits it to the special bank account.
82.example: Meera Textiles Private Limited is going through a winding up process. The Company Liquidator receives a cheque for payment from a customer. Instead of keeping the cheque in the office desk, the Liquidator must immediately take it and deposit it into the bank. The bank will then process the cheque, collect the money, and deposit those funds directly into the special bank account designated for the company.

terms.meaning: The person appointed to manage the closing down and selling off of a company's assets.
A financial instrument used in trade and credit, similar to a bill of exchange.
Documents that show ownership or a debt that must be paid, such as notes or bills.

82.watch: Note that this rule does not specify any exact time limit or deadline for the deposit, other than as soon as they come into the hands of the Liquidator.

83.summary: When the Tribunal orders someone to pay money owed to a company into a special bank account, that person must show a special document at the bank. They also need to inform the Company Liquidator and show them the bank receipt. This ensures that all payments are properly tracked during the winding up process.
points: You must pay the money into the special bank account managed by the Company Liquidator.
At the time of payment, you must show the bank a certified copy of the order or a challan signed by the Company Liquidator.
You must notify the Company Liquidator after making the payment.
You must show the bank receipt to the Company Liquidator.
83.example: The Tribunal ordered Ramesh to pay money owed to Alpha Electronics Private Limited into its special bank account. When Ramesh went to the bank to make the payment, he produced a certified copy of the Tribunal's order. After the payment was made, Ramesh immediately gave notice to the Company Liquidator, Mr. Sharma, and showed him the bank receipt to prove the payment was completed.

terms.meaning: A specialized legal body that handles company disputes and winding up cases.
The official person appointed to wind up the company and handle its assets.
An official form or document used for making a payment.

83.watch: Do not forget to both notify the Company Liquidator and show them the bank receipt after making the payment.

85.summary: This rule explains how a company liquidator can pay for necessary expenses when the company being wound up has no assets left. The liquidator can use government funds or money advanced by people involved in the case to cover costs. Later, these advanced funds must be repaid out of the company's assets before other debts are paid.
points: The Company Liquidator can use government advance funds to pay winding up expenses if the company has no assets, but needs permission from the Tribunal.
Expenses can also be paid using money advanced by the petitioner, a creditor, or a contributory.
Money used from government funds, common pools, or advanced by individuals must be repaid out of the company's assets before any other debts are cleared.
85.example: Meera Textiles Private Limited is being wound up by the Tribunal, but the company has no money or assets left to pay for the legal process. Rahul, a creditor, advances money to the Company Liquidator to cover these preliminary expenses. Later, when the company's assets are finally sold or collected, the Liquidator must repay Rahul first, giving his advance priority over all other debts owed by Meera Textiles Private Limited.

terms.meaning: The legal process of closing down a company and settling its affairs.
The person appointed to handle the closing down and sale of a company's assets.
A person liable to contribute to the assets of the company in the event of its being wound up.

85.watch: Do not assume that the liquidator can use government funds without asking the Tribunal first.

86.summary: This rule explains how extra company money not needed right away during a winding up must be invested. The Company Liquidator must place these funds in Government securities or interest-bearing scheduled bank deposits. When a fixed deposit matures, the Liquidator cannot renew it automatically and must check for better interest rates.
points: Surplus money not needed immediately must be invested in Government securities or scheduled bank interest-bearing deposits.
Investments must be in the name of the company and monitored regularly by the Company Liquidator.
Returns and fixed deposit details must be submitted to the Tribunal.
Matured fixed deposits cannot be automatically renewed; the Liquidator must check for higher interest rates elsewhere and report to the Tribunal.
86.example: Meera Textiles Private Limited is undergoing winding up. The Company Liquidator finds that Rs 5,00,000 is not needed right away. The Liquidator invests this surplus in an interest-bearing deposit in a scheduled bank under the company's name. After the deposit matures, the Liquidator checks other scheduled banks to see if a higher interest rate is available. Finding a better rate, the Liquidator reports this to the Tribunal and applies for permission to invest the funds in the new bank.

terms.meaning: The person appointed to run the winding up process of a company.
A bank listed in the second schedule of the Reserve Bank of India Act.
The judicial authority handling company law matters.

86.watch: A matured fixed deposit must not be automatically renewed without checking other banks for better interest rates.

87.summary: This rule tells the person winding up a company to check the account money every month. They must figure out if there is spare money to invest. They also need to write down their choice in a record book.
points: Check the liquidation account at the end of every single month.
Figure out if there is any money available to invest.
Write an entry in the company record book about checking the account and the decision made.
Write down the reasons if the choice is made not to invest extra money.
87.example: At the end of April, Mr. Roy, the Company Liquidator for Alpha Trades Private Limited, looked at the company liquidation account. He saw that there was spare money sitting in the account. He made an entry in the company record book to show he had checked the account and noted down his decision to invest the surplus funds. If he had decided not to invest, he would have written down his reasons in that same book.

terms.meaning: The person appointed to wind up and close down a company.
Extra money that is left over and available.

87.watch: Do not confuse this with a requirement to invest the money, as the rule only requires checking and recording the decision.

88.summary: This rule explains how a bank must handle investments for a company that is closing down. The bank can only make or sell these investments when the liquidator asks in writing. All securities are kept in the liquidator's name, and money from sales goes straight to their account.
points: The bank makes investments only on the written request of the Company Liquidator.
Securities are kept in the bank in the name and on behalf of the Company Liquidator.
The bank can only sell the securities under the written instructions of the Company Liquidator.
Money from sold securities must be credited by the bank to the Company Liquidator's account.
88.example: Meera Textiles Private Limited is winding up its business. The Company Liquidator wants to invest some surplus funds and sends a written request to the bank. The bank buys the securities and keeps them in the liquidator's name. Later, the liquidator gives written instructions to sell these securities. The bank sells them and credits the sale proceeds directly back into the Company Liquidator's account.

terms.meaning: The person appointed to run the winding up process and manage the assets of a company.
Financial investments like stocks or bonds.

88.watch: People often confuse who holds the securities, but they are kept by the bank while still being in the name of the Company Liquidator.

89.summary: This rule explains how money earned from investments and securities during a company winding up must be handled. The bank receives the earnings and deposits them into the Company Liquidator's account. Finally, the Company Liquidator credits this money to the specific company that owns the investment.
points: Banks must receive all dividends and interest from securities or investments.
The bank puts this money into the account of the Company Liquidator.
The bank must inform the Company Liquidator about the received money.
The Company Liquidator then credits this money to the correct company account.
89.example: Meera Textiles Private Limited is going through a winding up process and holds certain investments. The bank collects the interest generated from these investments and places it into the account of the Company Liquidator, Mr. Sharma. The bank immediately informs Mr. Sharma about this deposit. Following the rule, Mr. Sharma then credits the exact amount of interest into the specific account belonging to Meera Textiles Private Limited so the funds are correctly accounted for during the winding up.

terms.meaning: A share of profits paid by a company to its investors.
Financial instruments like stocks or bonds that hold monetary value.
The person officially appointed to wind up and close down a company.

89.watch: People often confuse who deposits the money first, but the bank must receive and credit it to the liquidator before the liquidator credits it to the company.

90.summary: The provided text is very short and simply states that the person winding up a company must claim any tax refunds that are due. It does not provide any further details, deadlines, or instructions. Therefore, the exact process cannot be fully explained from this text alone.
points: The Company Liquidator is responsible for claiming tax refunds.
This includes income-tax and any other taxes that are due to the company.
90.example: A company named Sunshine Paints Private Limited is being closed down. A person called the Company Liquidator is appointed to handle its remaining money and assets. While checking the records, the Liquidator finds that the company paid extra tax to the government in the past. Based on the rule, the Liquidator proceeds to claim this income-tax refund so the money can be recovered for the company.

terms.meaning: The person officially appointed to run the winding up process and close down a company.
Money that is paid back, such as extra tax paid to the government.

90.watch: People often confuse tax refunds with tax payments, but refunds are monies owed back to the company.

92.summary: This rule explains how a liquidator must present financial accounts when winding up a company. The account must show money received and paid out using specific official forms. Three copies of this account must be filed along with a sworn statement by the liquidator.
points: The account must be a statement of receipts and payments in Form WIN 39.
You must follow the instructions inside Form WIN 39 when preparing it.
Three copies of the account must be filed.
The Company Liquidator must verify the account using an affidavit in Form WIN 40.
The final account must be in Form WIN 41.
92.example: Meera Textiles Private Limited is winding up its business. The Company Liquidator, Mr. Sharma, prepares the financial statement of money received and paid out using Form WIN 39, following all the instructions given in that form. He makes three copies of this account and signs a sworn affidavit in Form WIN 40 to verify it. Finally, he submits the documents, and when the process concludes, he prepares the final account using Form WIN 41.

terms.meaning: The person appointed to manage the winding up and closing of a company.
A written statement confirmed by oath or affirmation for use as evidence.
A record of all the money that comes in and goes out.

92.watch: Do not forget to file three copies of the account along with the required affidavit.

93.summary: This rule explains what a Company Liquidator must do when there are no financial transactions during an accounting period. If the liquidator has not received or paid any money regarding the company's assets, they must submit a specific sworn statement. This statement must be filed on the exact date their regular accounts are due.
points: Applies when the Company Liquidator has received or paid zero money for company assets during the account period.
The liquidator must file an affidavit stating there are no receipts or payments.
The filing must happen on the date accounts are due.
93.example: Aarav is the Company Liquidator for Apex Goods Private Limited. During the latest accounting period, Aarav did not receive any money or pay out any funds related to the company's assets. Because of this rule, Aarav must file an affidavit stating there are no receipts or payments. He submits this affidavit on the exact date he is required to file his regular accounts for the period.

terms.meaning: The person appointed to wind up the affairs of a company.
A written statement confirmed by oath or affirmation for use as evidence.

93.watch: A common confusion is thinking that no financial activity means no paperwork needs to be filed at all.

95.summary: This rule explains how the accounts of a Company Liquidator must be checked. The Tribunal usually picks one or more Chartered Accountants from its own list to do a full check of these accounts. The liquidator must show all books, bills, and give any needed help and answers to the auditor.
points: The auditor is preferably a Chartered Accountant chosen by the Tribunal from an approved panel.
The audit is a complete check of the Company Liquidator's accounts.
The liquidator must provide all books and vouchers for the audit.
The liquidator must give the auditor all required explanations, information, and help.
95.example: Meera Textiles Private Limited is undergoing winding up, and Mr. Sharma is the Company Liquidator. The Tribunal appoints Ms. Gupta, a Chartered Accountant from the official panel, to check the accounts. Mr. Sharma gives Ms. Gupta all the account books, payment vouchers, and answers every question she asks so she can complete the full audit properly.

terms.meaning: A professional accountant who is officially certified to check financial accounts.
An official body or court that handles legal matters and disputes.
Receipts or papers that show proof of money spent or received.

95.watch: People often think the liquidator can choose any auditor, but the Tribunal actually appoints them from its own panel.

96.summary: When the Company Liquidator has their accounts audited, the auditor must send a certificate of the audit along with any comments to the Registry and the Liquidator. The Liquidator then files a copy of this certificate and the audited accounts with the Registrar of Companies. Finally, the Registry keeps the original audit certificate with the Tribunal records.
points: The auditor audits the Company Liquidator accounts filed in the Tribunal.
The auditor sends an audit certificate with comments to the Registry and the Company Liquidator.
The Company Liquidator files a copy of the audit certificate and audited accounts with the Registrar of Companies.
The Registry keeps the original audit certificate in the Tribunal records.
96.example: In a winding up proceeding for Meera Textiles Private Limited, an independent auditor reviews the accounts filed by the Company Liquidator. The auditor prepares an audit certificate with some comments and forwards one copy to the Registry and another copy to the Liquidator, named Mr. Sharma. Mr. Sharma then submits a copy of this audit certificate and the audited accounts to the Registrar of Companies. Meanwhile, the Registry safely places the original audit certificate among the official records of the Tribunal.

terms.meaning: The person appointed to wind up or close down a company.
The administrative office of the Tribunal.
The government office that maintains records of companies.

96.watch: Do not confuse the Tribunal's Registry with the Registrar of Companies, as they are two different offices receiving different copies.

97.summary: This rule explains how audit fees are decided during a company winding up process. The Tribunal determines these fees based on how complex or difficult the case is. The fees can also be adjusted over time as needed.
points: The Tribunal decides the audit fees.
Fees are fixed from time to time.
Decisions are based on the nature and complexity of the case.
97.example: In the case of Apex Technologies Private Limited, the winding up process involves sorting through tangled international accounts and numerous hidden assets. Because this situation is very complex and difficult to unravel, the Tribunal reviews the details and fixes the audit fees accordingly, ensuring the auditor is paid fairly for the difficult work involved.

terms.meaning: A special official body or court that handles specific legal disputes and cases.
The payment given to an auditor for checking and verifying financial records.

97.watch: Do not assume that the audit fees will stay the same throughout the entire case, as they can be fixed from time to time.

98.summary: This rule allows creditors and contributories to check the accounts and audit certificates during the winding up of a company. To do this, they must go to the office of the Tribunal and pay a specific fee. They can also get a copy of these documents by paying a charge per page.
points: Creditors and contributories have the right to inspect accounts and audit certificates.
Inspection takes place at the office of the Tribunal.
A fee of one hundred rupees must be paid for the inspection.
Copies of the documents can be obtained by paying five rupees per page.
98.example: Aarav is a creditor of ABC Enterprises Private Limited, which is currently going through a winding up process. Wishing to check the company's financial state, Aarav visits the office of the Tribunal. He pays the required fee of one hundred rupees to inspect the accounts and the auditor's certificate. Later, Aarav decides he needs a physical copy of the records to keep for his personal review, so he pays the additional charges at the rate of five rupees per page to obtain the copies.

terms.meaning: A person or company to whom money is owed.
A person liable to contribute to the assets of a company in the event of its being wound up.
A specialized legal body established to handle specific types of disputes, such as company law matters.

98.watch: Do not forget that both inspection and getting copies require separate, specific fee payments mentioned in the rule.

99.summary: This rule explains what happens after a company's accounts are audited during a winding up process. The Registry must take the audited statement and the auditor's certificate and show them to the Tribunal. The Tribunal will then consider them and pass necessary orders.
points: The accounts of the company are audited first.
The Registry places the statement of account before the Tribunal.
The auditor's certificate is also given to the Tribunal.
The Tribunal reviews these documents and gives orders.
99.example: Meera Textiles Private Limited is going through a winding up process. An auditor finishes checking the company's financial accounts and issues a formal certificate. Following the rules, the official Registry takes this statement of account and the auditor's certificate directly to the Tribunal. The Tribunal checks the documents to understand the financial situation and issues the next orders for the case.

terms.meaning: The administrative office of the court or Tribunal that handles paperwork and filings.
A special legal body or court set up to handle specific types of cases, such as company disputes and winding up.

99.watch: Do not assume this rule applies to summary winding up, as it falls under Part III for winding up by the Tribunal other than summary winding up.

103.summary: This rule explains what details must be included in a written statement when someone claims that a company owes them money during the winding up process. The person must use a specific form and give details about the debt, any bills or receipts, and whether they have special rights to be paid. This helps make sure all debt claims are clear and properly supported.
points: The claim must be made through a written statement on oath called an affidavit.
It must include an account statement showing the details of the debt and mention any supporting bills or vouchers.
It must state if the person is a secured or preferential creditor and give details of their security or claims.
The affidavit must be written in Form WIN 44.
103.example: Aarav wants to prove that Alpha Electronics Private Limited owes him money as the company winds up. He fills out Form WIN 44. In his affidavit, he includes an account statement detailing the exact debt and lists the delivery receipts as vouchers to prove it. He also mentions that he holds a special claim over some company equipment as security and explains those particulars clearly.

terms.meaning: A written statement confirmed by oath or affirmation for use as evidence.
A creditor who holds a security interest over the company's assets to protect their debt.
A creditor who has the right to be paid before other unsecured creditors by law.

103.watch: Make sure to use Form WIN 44 and clearly state whether you are a secured or preferential creditor.

104.summary: This rule makes it easier for many workers to claim unpaid wages from a company that is closing down. Instead of every single worker filing a separate claim, one person can file a single form for everyone. This group claim has the exact same legal effect as individual claims.
points: Applies when many workers have claims for unpaid wages or remuneration.
One person, such as a foreman, can file a single proof on behalf of all workers.
The claim form must include an attached schedule listing all workers and the amounts due to them.
This single filing has the same legal validity as separate claims made by each worker.
104.example: Meera Textiles Private Limited is closing down, and fifty factory workers are owed unpaid wages. Instead of fifty separate workers filling out individual paperwork, their supervisor, Ramesh, files a single Form WIN 45 on behalf of everyone. Ramesh attaches a schedule listing all fifty workers and the exact amounts owed to each person. Under this rule, Ramesh's single filing is treated as validly as if every single worker had submitted their own separate form.

terms.meaning: Workers and other people employed by the company.
Money paid for work or services, such as wages or salary.
A formal written document showing that a debt is owed.

104.watch: Do not assume that individual workers cannot file separately; the rule only says that filing together through one person is also sufficient.

105.summary: This rule explains what a creditor must do when they want to claim money from a company that is closing down. If the company owes money based on a financial paper like a promissory note, the creditor has to show it to the Company Liquidator. The Liquidator must then mark this paper before accepting the claim.
points: A creditor must show the financial paper to prove their claim.
The rule applies to bills of exchange, promissory notes, and similar negotiable instruments.
The Company Liquidator must mark the document before the claim is accepted.
105.example: Meera Textiles Private Limited is winding up its business. Creditor Rohan holds a promissory note signed by the company to prove a debt owed to him. To have his claim officially admitted, Rohan brings this promissory note to the Company Liquidator. The Liquidator inspects the document, marks it appropriately, and then admits Rohan's proof of debt.

terms.meaning: A person or company to whom money is owed.
A signed document containing a written promise to pay a stated sum to a specified person.
The official person appointed to wind up or close down the company.

105.watch: Do not assume this rule applies without showing the actual physical or electronic document to the Liquidator.

106.summary: This rule explains how to decide the value of debts and claims against a company during a winding up. Normally, the value is estimated as of the date the provisional liquidator is appointed or the winding up order is made, whichever comes first. However, if the company passed a resolution to wind up before the winding up petition was presented, that resolution date is used instead.
points: Debts and claims are estimated as of the earlier of the provisional liquidator's appointment or the winding up order.
If the company passed a winding up resolution before the petition was presented, the resolution date is used for estimation.
106.example: Meera Textiles Private Limited faced financial trouble. On March 1, the company passed a resolution to wind up voluntarily. Later, a formal winding up petition was presented, and a winding up order was made on June 1. Because the company passed its winding up resolution before the petition was presented, all debts and claims against Meera Textiles Private Limited must be estimated according to their value on March 1, which was the date of the resolution.

terms.meaning: A temporary person appointed to take charge of a company's property and affairs before a final winding up order is made.
The legal process of closing down a company, settling its debts, and distributing any remaining assets.

106.watch: People often get confused about which date to use when a company passes a resolution before the winding up petition is filed.

107.summary: This rule tells creditors how to calculate the exact amount of debt they are claiming from a company that is closing down. Creditors must subtract any trade discounts from the total debt amount before they prove it. The text is very short, so it only covers this single instruction.
points: A creditor must prove their debt.
The creditor is required to deduct all trade discounts from the debt.
107.example: Meera Textiles Private Limited is winding up its business. A supplier named Rahul claims the company owes him money for goods. When Rahul submits his proof of debt to the company, he checks his invoices. Because the invoices included trade discounts, Rahul properly subtracts those discounts from his total claim before submitting it to the liquidator, following the required rule.

terms.meaning: A person or business that is owed money.
A reduction in the price of goods given by a seller to a buyer.

107.watch: Do not forget to subtract all trade discounts before you submit your debt proof.

108.summary: This rule explains how a creditor can claim interest on a debt when a company is winding up. If no interest was previously agreed upon, the creditor can still claim interest up to six percent per year or an amount decided by the Tribunal. The exact starting point for calculating this interest depends on whether the debt had a fixed written due date or required a written demand.
points: Creditors can claim interest on overdue debts even if no interest was originally agreed.
The maximum interest rate is six percent per year unless the Tribunal decides otherwise.
For debts with a written due date, interest starts from when the debt was payable.
For other debts, interest starts from the date of a written demand for interest.
108.example: Meera Textiles Private Limited went into winding up, leaving an unpaid debt to ABC Supplies. They had a written contract stating the bill was due on a specific date, but the contract did not mention interest. Because the debt was overdue, ABC Supplies decided to claim interest under the rules. They asked for interest at the rate of six percent per year, starting from the original due date stated in their written contract up to the date of the winding up order.

terms.meaning: The legal process of closing down a company and settling its affairs.
A specialized legal body that handles company law disputes in India.
A formal written document, such as a contract or agreement.

108.watch: Do not assume interest is always six percent, as the Tribunal has the power to decide a different rate.

109.summary: This rule is about how regular payments like rent are handled when a company is ordered to shut down, known as winding up. If a payment is due over time, people can claim a fair share of it up to the exact date of the winding up order. However, if the company liquidator keeps using a rented space, the landlord can still claim rent for the time of that occupation.
points: Rent or other payments are calculated proportionally up to the winding up date.
This applies when the winding up order happens between normal payment due dates.
The landlord keeps the right to claim rent for the period the liquidator stays in the premises.
109.example: Meera Textiles Private Limited rented a building from Mr. Sharma. The monthly rent was due on the first of every month. On the tenth of the month, the company received a winding up order. Under this rule, Mr. Sharma is entitled to rent for those ten days. Furthermore, because the Company Liquidator kept using the building after that date, Mr. Sharma can also claim rent for the entire duration of the liquidator's occupation.

terms.meaning: The process of closing down a company and settling its affairs.
The person appointed to manage the closing down of the company.
Rented or leased out property.

109.watch: Do not assume that closing the company stops the obligation to pay rent if the liquidator continues to use the rented space.

110.summary: This rule allows a creditor to claim a future debt during a company winding up as if it were due right now. The creditor can receive dividends just like other creditors, but a small interest deduction is made for early payment. This ensures fair treatment for debts that were not yet due when the winding up order was made.
points: Creditors can claim future debts as if they are payable right now during winding up.
They receive dividends equally with other creditors.
An interest rebate of six percent per year is deducted from the dividend.
The interest period is calculated from the dividend declaration date to the original payment due date.
110.example: Alpha Logistics Private Limited is winding up. Supplier Rohan is owed a payment that was only supposed to become due six months later. Under this rule, Rohan can claim the money now and receive dividends alongside other creditors. However, a rebate of interest at six per cent per annum is deducted from the dividend, calculated from the dividend declaration date until the future date when the debt was originally due to be paid.

terms.meaning: The legal process of closing down a company and settling its affairs.
Payments made to creditors or shareholders from the company's available funds.
A deduction or discount taken from an amount.

110.watch: Do not forget that the six percent interest rebate applies only to the time between the dividend declaration and the future due date.

111.summary: The Company Liquidator must check every debt claim submitted by creditors. This must be done within thirty days or within the time allowed by the Tribunal. The liquidator can ask for more documents or ask the creditor to attend in person.
points: The liquidator must examine every proof of debt and its grounds as soon as possible.
The process must happen within thirty days or a time allowed by the Tribunal.
The liquidator can demand documentary proof or further evidence.
If the liquidator needs more evidence or a personal visit, they must fix a date and time.
A notice in Form WIN 46 must be sent by registered or speed post at least seven days before the date.
111.example: Meera Textiles Private Limited is undergoing winding up. Creditor Rohan submits a proof of debt claiming the company owes him money for fabric supply. The Company Liquidator examines the claim and needs more details. The liquidator asks Rohan to provide extra delivery receipts and to attend an investigation in person. The liquidator sends a notice in Form WIN 46 to Rohan by speed post, making sure it reaches Rohan at least seven days before the scheduled date.

terms.meaning: The person appointed to handle the winding up and closing of a company.
A formal statement or document showing that a company owes money to someone.
The judicial authority that handles company law disputes and cases in India.

111.watch: Make sure to send the notice so that it actually reaches the creditor at least seven days before the meeting, not just dispatch it seven days prior.

112.summary: During a company closure, the person in charge called the Company Liquidator can ask anyone for information about debts and documents. The Liquidator must pay for their travel expenses when making this request. If the person refuses to show up or hides from the notice, the Liquidator can report them to the Tribunal for orders.
points: The Company Liquidator can ask any person for information about debts.
The Liquidator can also demand documents related to those debts.
Travel and other expenses must be paid to the person when they are called.
If someone avoids the notice or fails to attend without a lawful excuse, the Liquidator can report it to the Tribunal.
112.example: Alpha Logistics Limited is going through liquidation. The Company Liquidator believes that Mr. Sharma holds important documents regarding company debts. The Liquidator sends a call to Mr. Sharma along with money to cover his travel expenses. Mr. Sharma ignores the call and avoids receiving the notice. Because of this, the Liquidator reports Mr. Sharma to the Tribunal to get appropriate orders against him.

terms.meaning: The person appointed to manage the closing and winding up of a company.
A specialized legal authority or court that handles company law cases.
The process of bringing a company to an end and settling its debts.

112.watch: People sometimes think they can ignore the call if they are busy, but failing to attend without a lawful excuse allows the Liquidator to report them to the Tribunal.

113.summary: This rule allows the Company Liquidator to take affidavits when checking proof of debts. The Liquidator can choose to skip this requirement if they wish. They also have the power to accept an affidavit or a formal undertaking instead of a formal oath.
points: The Company Liquidator may take affidavits for admitting proof of debts.
The Liquidator has the discretion to skip taking an affidavit entirely.
The Liquidator can allow an affidavit or an undertaking instead of an oath.
113.example: In a winding up proceeding for Meera Textiles Private Limited, a creditor named Mr. Sharma submits a claim for unpaid goods. To verify this debt, the Company Liquidator decides to use his power under the rules. Instead of asking for a traditional oath, the Liquidator allows Mr. Sharma to submit a signed undertaking to confirm that his debt claim is true and correct.

terms.meaning: A written statement confirmed by oath or affirmation for use as evidence.
A formal promise or agreement to do something.
The process of showing and proving the money owed by the company.

113.watch: Do not assume that affidavits are always mandatory, as the Liquidator has the power to dispense with them.

114.summary: This rule explains who pays the expenses for proving that a company owes money. Unless the Tribunal orders otherwise, the person claiming the debt must pay these costs themselves. This ensures creditors handle their own proof expenses during winding up.
points: Creditors must bear the costs of proving their debt.
The Tribunal has the power to order a different arrangement.
114.example: Aarav runs a printing press that provided stationery to Alpha Tech Private Limited before it went into liquidation. To claim his unpaid bills, Aarav submits a proof of debt to the Tribunal. According to the rules, Aarav must pay for any expenses he incurs while preparing and submitting this proof, unless the Tribunal specifically orders otherwise.

terms.meaning: A person or company to whom money is owed.
The judicial body handling company law cases and disputes.

114.watch: Do not assume the company will automatically reimburse your costs for proving a debt.

116.summary: If a creditor is unhappy with a liquidator's decision about their claim, they can appeal to the Tribunal within twenty-one days of receiving notice. The appeal needs a specific form, an affidavit explaining the reasons, and notice given to the liquidator. The Tribunal will then handle the appeal with the powers of an appellate court.
points: A creditor can appeal if they are unhappy with the Company Liquidator's decision on their proof.
The appeal must be filed within twenty-one days from the date the notice of the decision is served.
The appeal requires Form WIN 49 and a supporting affidavit that states the grounds for the appeal.
Notice of the appeal must be given to the Company Liquidator.
116.example: Meera Textiles Private Limited was undergoing winding up, and a creditor, Ramesh, submitted his proof of debt. The Company Liquidator rejected part of Ramesh's claim. Dissatisfied with this choice, Ramesh decided to challenge it. Within twenty-one days of receiving the liquidator's notice, Ramesh filed an appeal using Form WIN 49. He included a supporting affidavit detailing his reasons and properly notified the Company Liquidator so the Tribunal could review the matter.

terms.meaning: A person or company to whom money is owed.
A written statement confirmed by oath or affirmation for use as evidence in court.
A specialized official body set up to deal with and decide legal disputes.

116.watch: Remember that the twenty-one day deadline starts from the date the notice is served to the creditor, not from any other date.

117.summary: This rule explains what happens when a creditor appeals a decision to reject their proof of debt. The Company Liquidator must send the proof and rejection reasons to the Registry. Other creditors or contributors can also ask the Tribunal for permission to join the appeal.
points: The Company Liquidator must file the rejected proof and its rejection order with the Registry upon receiving notice of an appeal.
Creditors and contributories can apply to the Tribunal for permission to intervene in the appeal.
The Tribunal may grant permission to intervene with specific terms and conditions.
If permission is granted, notice of the appeal hearing must be given to that creditor or contributory.
117.example: Meera Textiles Private Limited is undergoing winding up. A creditor, Rohan, appeals because his proof of debt was rejected. Upon receiving the appeal notice, the Company Liquidator files Rohan's proof and the rejection grounds with the Registry. Meanwhile, another creditor, Sunita, applies to the Tribunal for permission to intervene in the appeal. The Tribunal grants her leave to join, and ensures she receives notice of the upcoming hearing.

terms.meaning: A document showing that a company owes money to a creditor.
A person who is liable to contribute to the assets of a company in the event of its being wound up.
To join an ongoing legal proceeding or case.

117.watch: Note that this rule only applies after an appeal has been filed against a rejected proof.

118.summary: The rules state that a Company Liquidator does not have to pay the costs out of their own pocket if someone appeals their decision to reject a proof. This protection applies when the liquidator has rejected a proof either completely or partially. It ensures they are not held personally responsible for the expenses of such legal challenges.
points: The Company Liquidator is never personally liable for costs.
This applies to costs arising from an appeal.
The appeal must be against the liquidator's decision to reject a proof wholly or in part.
118.example: Meera Textiles Private Limited is undergoing winding up, and Arun is appointed as the Company Liquidator. A creditor submits a claim proof, which Arun rejects in part. The creditor decides to file an appeal against Arun's decision in court. Because of the rules, Arun does not have to pay any legal costs out of his own pocket for defending this appeal.

terms.meaning: A person appointed to wind up the affairs of a company.
A document or evidence showing a claim against the company.

118.watch: Do not assume this protects the liquidator from personal liability in all matters outside of appeals concerning rejected proofs.

119.summary: This rule requires the Company Liquidator to file a list of creditors in the Tribunal within thirty days of the date fixed for submitting proofs. The Liquidator must show the claim amounts and clearly state which claims were accepted, partially accepted or rejected. Along with this list, the Liquidator must also file the actual proof documents and a certificate.
points: The Company Liquidator must file a list of creditors in Form WIN 50.
The filing must happen within thirty days from the date fixed for submitting proofs, unless the Tribunal gives more time.
The list must show the debt amounts and specify whether each claim was accepted, partly accepted, or rejected.
The proofs of claims with admission or rejection notes must be filed in the Tribunal along with a certificate.
119.example: In the winding up of Meera Textiles Private Limited, the Company Liquidator set a deadline for creditors to submit their claims. After receiving the claims, the Liquidator prepared a list in Form WIN 50 showing the debt amounts and which claims were approved or rejected. Within thirty days from the submission date, the Liquidator filed this list, along with the claim proofs and a certificate, in the Tribunal.

terms.meaning: The person appointed to handle the closing down and winding up of a company.
The official legal body or court handling company law matters.
A document showing evidence of a debt owed by the company.

119.watch: Do not assume the Tribunal cannot extend the thirty-day deadline, because the rule allows the Tribunal to grant further time.

120.summary: This rule explains that the list of creditors filed in the Tribunal is the official list for the company.
